notes:
A respectful, somewhat literary term for an elderly woman. Commonly found in novels, news reports, and formal descriptions. Carries more dignity than casual terms like ⟦おばあさん→おばあさん：02863_obaasan⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{老婦人|ろうふじん}: an elderly woman (narrative style)
- ⟦{上品|じょうひん}→上品：03081_jouhin⟧な{老婦人|ろうふじん}: an elegant elderly woman
- {老婦人|ろうふじん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{語|かた}る→語る：01930_kataru⟧: an elderly woman tells/recounts

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦おばあさん→おばあさん：02863_obaasan⟧: grandmother, old woman — casual and warm; the everyday word
- ⟦{老女|ろうじょ}→老女：14017_roujo⟧: old woman — literary but less polite than {老婦人|ろうふじん}
- {老紳士|ろうしんし}: elderly gentleman — the male counterpart with a similarly dignified tone
- ご⟦{婦人|ふじん}→婦人：01658_fujin⟧: lady — polite term for a woman of any age, often middle-aged or older

REGISTER:
Formal and literary. Appears in novels, newspaper articles, and polite descriptions. Not typically used in casual conversation.

ETYMOLOGY:
Composed of {老|ろう} (old, elderly) + ⟦{婦人|ふじん}→婦人：01658_fujin⟧ (woman, lady).

definitions.explanation: a polite or literary term for an elderly woman
